gaps.sentence: What ___ pity that the show closed so soon.
gaps.explanation: 'What a pity' is the fixed exclamatory phrase.

gaps.sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: ___ sales figures for October look promising.
gaps.explanation: 'The sales figures for October' — defined by the for-phrase.

gaps.sentence: He gave me ___ useful advice about the paperwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — never 'an advice'. Use 'a piece of advice' for one item.

gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).

gaps.sentence: ___ influenza, or flu, is highly contagious.
gaps.explanation: Most disease names take no article: influenza, flu, malaria (compare: the flu is also heard informally).

gaps.sentence: ___ noise pollution in cities is getting worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Noise pollution' as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ Smith family have lived in this street since 1990.
gaps.explanation: 'The Smith family' — the whole family takes 'the'.
